attribution.note: The preceding sentence attributes an analogy to Carl Brown; Zitron directly asserts the subsequent slowdown claim himself.

semantics.note: The statement asserts that coding LLM use causes slower engineering work, without an explicit population or task restriction.

contract.note: Actual completion time fairly operationalizes speed. The contract appropriately recognizes opposite causal effects across controlled settings.

evidence.note: The randomized METR study reports 19% longer completion times for experienced maintainers on familiar projects, supporting slowdown in that setting.
Google's own randomized study reports approximately 21% shorter task times. This is company-authored evidence with a large confidence interval and limited generalizability.

reviews.rationale: Experienced maintainers slowed down in the METR trial, while Google engineers sped up in a different controlled setting. Under the contract, these opposing effects warrant mixed: slowdown holds in one setting, but the unconditional denial of speedups does not. Neither study establishes an industry-wide average.

Anthropic reports ongoing government adoption immediately before the cutoff. This does not independently establish sector health or settle the unlimited forecast.
